title: Normalized inverse image of the nonnegative coefficient lines
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and completed coefficient sheaves $R_T=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $g^*_{\rm mod}$ be the ordinary coefficient-linear module pullback, with the canonical completed coefficient comparison [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback], and write $\iota_g(x)$ for its specified adjunction-unit image of a section $x$ over $V$ as a section over $g^*V$. Let $L_T(0)=R_T$, $L_T(1)=\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_T\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T}(\mathcal O_E)_T$, and $L_T(d)=L_T(1)^{\otimes d}$ for $d>0$, with the published tensor-power parenthesization [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Roots of unity and their inverse-limit pullback maps are those of [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf, def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image]. For a scalar $a$ and $d$ root-tower sections $x_1,\ldots,x_d$, denote their pure coefficient tensor by $t_d(a;x_1,\ldots,x_d)$; $t_0(a)=a$.

There is a unique family of module isomorphisms $\tau_d:g^*_{\rm mod}L_Y(d)\cong L_X(d)$, $d\geq0$, such that, over every base-change object $g^*V$, $\tau_d(\iota_g(t_d(a;x_1,\ldots,x_d)))=t_d(c_g(a);g^*x_1,\ldots,g^*x_d)$, where $c_g$ is the specified completed coefficient map and $g^*x_j$ is the inverse-limit root comparison applied to its inverse-image unit. In particular the degree-zero comparison sends the unit-section image of $1$ to $1$. No finite-field datum or Weil structure is a hypothesis.

source.place: Natural Weil isomorphism on coefficient twists; the explicit sheaf-level and derived normalization and complete proof are already recorded in lean/Sheaf/Paper/FrobeniusCoefficientTwistsCanonical.lean at WeilConjectures.FrobeniusCoefficientTwists.existsUnique_positiveLineMaps, WeilConjectures.FrobeniusCoefficientTwists.positiveLineMaps. The general construction is the one in these existing declarations, with the isomorphism-derived-pullback normalization cited there.

proof.text: The covering-preserving pro-etale site equivalence transports the root-of-unity comparisons and all their power transition maps. Inverse image commutes with inverse limits, so their limit is the root-tower comparison. It is invertible for a scheme isomorphism.

Use the canonical completed coefficient comparison on scalars. Extend the root comparison across the constant coefficient rings to obtain the map on L(1), and tensor these maps with the published parenthesization for every positive d. The inverse-image tensor comparison makes all these maps linear and invertible. At d=0 use the completed regular-module comparison. The displayed formulas follow on the coefficient and root generators.

Sectionwise balanced tensor products are generated by pure tensors, and sheafification preserves their universal property. Thus two linear maps satisfying the formulas coincide locally and hence globally. For d=0, a linear map from the regular module is determined by the image of 1. This proves uniqueness, including d=0 and the empty scheme.

theorem existsUnique_positiveLineMaps (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso g] :
    ∃! tau : ∀ d : ℕ,
      (modulePull l E g).obj (positiveLine l E Y d) ≅
        positiveLine l E X d,
      ∀ (d : ℕ) (V : Y.ProEt)
        (a : (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted
          l E Y).obj.obj (op V))
        (x : Fin d → (purTwistZlOne Y l).obj.obj (op V)),
        (tau d).hom.val.app (op ((proEtaleBaseChange g).obj V))
            (moduleSection l E g (positiveLine l E Y d) V
              (generator l E Y (op V) a d x)) =
          generator l E X (op ((proEtaleBaseChange g).obj V))
            ((sfCompletedCoefficientMap l E g).hom.app (op V) a)
            d (fun i ↦ rootSection l g V (x i))
